title: Three Years and One Short Tool
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：priority　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 priority 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the craftsman ① set the priority that no apprentice in the workshop would have measured, and he said the setting was the whole of the year. The ② priority, meaning the rank itself and not the tool, ran three years and stayed unmeasured in the book; a priority, he said, is the only thing in a workshop that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ priority in that workshop had the same short tool beside it, and the ④ priority at the far bench, meaning the order they kept for the children to finish and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A priority, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the craftsman said the measuring is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the priority was the whole of the matter, meaning the importance and not the rank. The ⑥ priority, meaning the importance and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; priority, he said, is either something you set or the only word that means both a rank and an importance. He said the importance is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ priority had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the short tool. The ⑧ priority of the whole thing, the craftsman wrote in August, was one workshop and three years of measuring; priority, he said, is either the order at the far bench or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ priority I remember is the rank measured in the ledger, which closed in 1967 and is still measured as the quietest in the workshop. A ⑩ priority, my mother said in 1969, is the only rank that improves by being measured; every priority, she said, is an importance that has agreed to look like a rank. She said the importance was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 优先；优先事项（指工坊里每一项旁边的那一项）
B. n. 优先；优先事项（指那项优先本身，与小小的工具相对）
C. 固定搭配：set the priority 排定这一项优先
D. n. 优先；优先事项（指留给孩子们赶完的那一桩）
E. n. 优先之事（抽象总称，指一处工坊的优先之事）
F. n. 优先；优先事项（指工料簿里写到、被测量的那一项）
G. n. 优先、轻重（指一件事里人人都做却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 轻重（抽象总称，指人人都做却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: set the priority that no apprentice in the workshop would have measured
The priority, meaning the rank itself and not the tool
the priority at the far bench
the priority was the whole of the matter
the priority had become a line in a ledger
The priority of the whole thing
A priority, my mother said in 1969

answers.why: set the priority 意为“排定这一项优先”，1960 年那位匠人把工坊里没有一位学徒肯测量的一项优先做了一遍。
priority 意为“优先；优先事项”，指那项优先本身而不是小小的工具，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被测量。
priority 意为“优先；优先事项”，指工坊里每一项旁边的那一项，每一项旁边都有同一件小小的工具。
priority 意为“优先；优先事项”，指最远那张案台的留给孩子们赶完的那一桩，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
priority 意为“优先、轻重”，指一件事里人人都做却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这项轻重就是那件事的全部。
priority 意为“轻重”，指人人都做却无人提起的那样东西而不是那项优先，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
priority 意为“优先；优先事项”，指工料簿里写到、被测量的那一项，到 1965 年这一项成了工料簿里的一行。
priority 意为“优先之事”，匠人八月写道，整件事的优先之事是一处工坊和三个年头的测量。
priority 意为“优先；优先事项”，我记得的是工料簿里测量过的那一项，1967 年出师了，至今仍被说成工坊里最安静的一项。
priority 为抽象总称，母亲 1969 年说，优先是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的优先。
